title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 58 (Refusal of Registration and Appeal Against Refusal)

content.overview: Section 58 provides that if a private company limited by shares refuses to register a transfer or transmission of shares, it must send notice of refusal to the transferor and transferee (or person giving intimation of transmission) within thirty days of the date on which the instrument or intimation was delivered. Public companies generally may not refuse registration of transfer of securities. Aggrieved persons may appeal to the Tribunal within the prescribed period; the Tribunal may direct registration or confirm refusal and give consequential directions.
content.glance: Private company: notice of refusal within 30 days; public company: generally no refusal of transfer; appeal to Tribunal; Tribunal may direct registration or confirm refusal.
content.study: If a private company limited by shares refuses, whether in pursuance of any power under its articles or otherwise, to register the transfer of, or the transmission by operation of law of the right to, any securities or interest of a member, it must within thirty days from the date on which the instrument of transfer or the intimation of transmission was delivered to the company, send notice of the refusal to the transferor and the transferee or to the person giving intimation of transmission. Without prejudice to other remedies, the transferor or transferee or the person who gave intimation may appeal to the Tribunal against the refusal within the prescribed period. A public company generally shall not refuse registration of transfer of securities. On appeal, the Tribunal may direct that the transfer or transmission be registered or that the refusal be confirmed, and may give incidental and consequential directions. Current-law framing: identify private vs public company; check notice timeline; apply appeal to Tribunal and possible orders.

sections.heading: Private Company Refusal
sections.body: If a private company refuses to register transfer or transmission, it must send notice of refusal within thirty days of delivery of the instrument or intimation.

sections.heading: Public Company
sections.body: A public company shall not refuse registration of transfer of securities (subject to the Act).

sections.heading: Appeal to Tribunal
sections.body: Aggrieved transferor, transferee or transmission applicant may appeal to the Tribunal within the prescribed period.

sections.heading: Tribunal Powers
sections.body: Tribunal may direct registration or confirm refusal and give incidental and consequential directions including as to costs and damages.

provisions.title: Refusal of registration and appeal against refusal

examples.title: Private company refusal notice
examples.body: A private company refuses a transfer under its articles and sends notice within thirty days. The transferee may appeal to the Tribunal under s. 58.

examples.title: Public company refusal
examples.body: A public company refuses to register a duly completed transfer without statutory ground. Section 58’s general bar on public company refusal is engaged; the aggrieved party may appeal.

hypotheticals.question: Does a private company have unlimited power to refuse registration?
hypotheticals.analysis: It may refuse under its articles or otherwise, but must give notice within thirty days, and the refusal is subject to Tribunal appeal under s. 58.

distinctions.title: Refusal of registration (s. 58) vs transfer procedure (s. 56)
distinctions.left: When registration may be refused and how to challenge

misconceptions.trap: Public companies may freely refuse transfers like private companies.
misconceptions.correction: Section 58 generally prohibits public companies from refusing registration of transfer of securities.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 58 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify private or public company. II. Check refusal and 30-day notice. III. Assess appeal to Tribunal. IV. State possible orders. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Company type; refusal facts; notice compliance; appeal grounds; precise relief.

caseLaw.point: A refusal to register a transfer must be in the interest of the company and for a reason the articles permit. A blanket refusal is not enough.
